open_decisions_resolved: Filename source-identity encoding: sure_dataset mixes videoN_frame_MMMM.jpg (source-encoded) with a pooled contiguous plain frame_MMMM.jpg range (0000-0034), confirmed byte-identical via md5 to data/frames/ files of the same name -- treated as one pooled source group 'frame_source0'.
imagehash library availability: NOT installed in anaconda env (import fails) -- implemented minimal 64-bit aHash + dHash inline with PIL+numpy only, exactly per the design doc's own fallback plan.
notes: Strong criterion (zero cross-split leakage) NOT met: perceptual hashing found 32 near-duplicate candidate pairs at a strict threshold, 14 of which are literally adjacent frame indices (gap=1) of the same source video split across train/val -- a real temporal-adjacency leakage risk distinct from and milder than the already-excluded ogretmen case (no exact-duplicate frames; 0/0 exact index overlaps). Minimum-viable criterion met: affected videos and exact file pairs are fully enumerated in exp05_summary.json. Recommend the paper add an explicit caveat to headline vision metrics rather than claim a fully clip-disjoint split.

open_decisions_resolved: Full-frame-miss estimation approach: implemented direct empirical count (primary) via best.pt inference on actual val frames at the deployed threshold, plus the independence approximation as a secondary sanity-check, per the design doc's own recommendation.

Confidence sweep points: read vision-service/yolo_runner.py directly, found CONF_THRESH=0.20 (not the assumed 0.25 default) with an inline comment confirming it was deliberately lowered from 0.30 for recall -- swept {0.10,0.15,0.20,0.25,0.30,0.35,0.40} around the confirmed deployed value.
notes: Two findings beyond the original hypothesis, both important for the write-up: (1) the val set contains NO frames with 1-2 fish (minimum is k=3) -- the sparse-frame regime H7 worried about is entirely untested by this dataset, not merely 'found to be rare'; extrapolated (untested) independence-approximation miss risk at k=1 is ~22-28% depending on which recall figure is used, a real quantified gap to flag. (2) model.val(conf=X) does NOT pin box.mp/box.mr to conf=X for X below the internal argmax (methodological trap, documented) -- reading the fine-grained per-confidence curve directly revealed the DEPLOYED operating point (conf=0.20) actually runs at P=0.720/R=0.782, not the headline P=0.858/R=0.719. Production recall is thus HIGHER (more reassuring for full-frame-miss risk) than the number the paper has been citing for this discussion; the paper's H7 section should cite the deployed-point recall (0.782), not the academic-argmax headline (0.719), when discussing real-world full-frame-miss risk.
